- When sentiment turns positive after a negative trend, model tends to overreact and overshoot — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overcorrects downward — adjust downward bias by 3–5% of the spike magnitude.
- If sentiment change is negative and news volume is low, model underreacts — increase forecast slightly to reflect muted market sentiment.
- If sentiment change is positive and news volume is high, model underestimates upside — raise forecast by 2–5% to capture momentum.
- Model consistently underestimates true price when sentiment is flat or mildly negative — add 1–3% to forecast to account for mean reversion bias.
- Forecast horizon 30d often lags true price by 1–3 days — adjust for lag by adding 0.5–1.5% per day of delay.
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid changes), model overfits short-term noise — smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values.
